variants.name: Helios-44 (earliest, Start bayonet)
variants.tell: silver barrel, 13-blade preset diaphragm, on the Zenit Start's own bayonet mount (not M39) — the rarest, most sought-after generation

variants.name: Helios-44 (M39 Zenit-thread, early)
variants.tell: 13-blade preset diaphragm, single-layer coating, on the Zenit 1/3/3M M39 SLR thread (not Leica/LTM M39)

variants.name: Helios-44 'Zebra' (M39 Zenit-thread)
variants.tell: black body with chrome/silver stripes on the focus ring, gold-tinted coating instead of violet — BelOMO, late 1960s

variants.name: Helios-44 (M39 Zenit-thread, later)
variants.tell: 8-blade preset — later runs of the same M39 generation dropped blade count from 13
M42, preset two-ring mechanism, all-metal, no stop-down pin — the collector 'reference' preset Helios-44

variants.name: 44M / 44M-4 to 44M-7
variants.tell: auto-aperture via spring-loaded rear pin; higher M number = later coating/blade generation (8→6 blades from 44M-4 on)

variants.name: original Soviet production
variants.tell: KMZ-made, 1969–early 1990s

variants.name: modern reissue (Zenit brand)
variants.tell: back in production 2013–present under the Zenit brand — sold new, not a vintage example

variants.name: original 'automat' mount
variants.tell: pre-Nikon-F-mount version of the lens

variants.name: 81N (Nikon F-derived 'H'/'N' bayonet)
variants.tell: close copy of Nikon F, incompatible with several AI-S Nikon bodies (FA, F-301, F-501, F4) without modification; renamed Arsat-H/Arsat-N after 1991

variants.name: collapsible barrel
variants.tell: barrel retracts into the mount for storage — mainly LZOS-made

variants.name: rigid barrel
variants.tell: fixed non-collapsible barrel, alongside the collapsible version — KMZ-made

variants.name: coated (1949 on)
variants.tell: red 'P' ring marking on the front ring

variants.name: uncoated (1948 only)
variants.tell: no coating, no red ring — earliest production only

variants.name: with focusing lever
variants.tell: small lever tab on the focus ring for one-handed adjustment

variants.name: focus ring only (no lever)
variants.tell: ring sits directly against the mount, awkward to turn — no lever tab

variants.name: black finish
variants.tell: black-painted barrel

variants.name: silver/chrome finish
variants.tell: bare polished metal barrel — both finishes exist, no confirmed date-range split between them

variants.name: Industar-96U-1
variants.tell: same optical formula, different body/housing design — produced from 1985

variants.name: Type 1 (1950s)
variants.tell: silver barrel, infinity lock

variants.name: Type 2 (1960s)
variants.tell: silver barrel, no infinity lock

variants.name: Type 3 (1970s)
variants.tell: black barrel, white numbers

variants.name: Type 4 (1980s-91)
variants.tell: black barrel, green and white numbers

variants.name: single-coated (original)
variants.tell: 1951-1970s production, no visible multicoat tint

variants.name: MC (multi-coated)
variants.tell: 1980s+ production, visible blue-green multicoating

variants.name: Tair-3A
variants.tell: standalone tripod-mount barrel; sold with yellow/orange filters, hood, and quiver case (general-purpose retail kit, not Photosniper-bundled)

variants.name: Brussels Grand Prix export marking
variants.tell: engraved "MIR-1 ... GRAND PRIX BRUSSELS 1958" in English on export-marked examples

variants.name: single-coated (1973-1989)
variants.tell: original coating era

variants.name: MC / Mir-20M (1989+)
variants.tell: multi-coated, marked "Mir-20M" or "MC Mir-20M" on the barrel
